To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the temperature and water table can be independently controlled in a laboratory sediment column, and that this design allows simulation of subsurface conditions that are representative of seasonal variation in the deep vadoe zone and capillary fring.

a 2.0 m tall laboratory column was capable of generating temperature profiles that encompassed the full range of temperatures observed in the deep soil and capillary fringe at a site in the semiarid Colorado River floodplain, and that the water table was varied to represent seasonal conditions.

a sediment column was designed to allow laboratory simulation of thermal profiles found in the deep vadoe zone and capillary fringes of field settings, and the column was capable of generating profiles of temperature, water content, and matric potential that are representative of seasonal conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of a laboratory apparatus for simulating subsurface temperature and water content profiles in sediment column studies.
the development of an experimental approach to investigate subsurface biogerochemical processes in a controlled laboratory environment.
the development of a laboratory sediment column that simulates the temperature and water table conditions of subsurface environments.

the authors have developed a new and useful method for controlling temperature profiles in laboratory sediment columns, and they have demonstrated the method's utility in a study of subsurface carbon dioxide dynamics.

this study provides a method to simulate realistic subsurface biogeochmical conditions in the laboratory.

the column is a very useful tool for studying biogeochemical reactions under different temperature profiles.

it is important to control temperature in the laboratory to mimic natural conditions.
